description:
fz-kdt.104 dropped runtime-unroutable alternatives at callsite_dispatch::call_destinations. Its sibling constructor, dispatch_from_callable_flow_edges (same file), builds the CallableConstructionFact selection plan the same way -- one row per first-class callable-flow edge, questions projected through runtime_type_test_envelope -- and carries the same defect: two edges whose surfaces project to ONE RuntimeTypePredicate are not two alternatives, and their order is the scheduler(s).

MEASURED AT FIFO, 577-fixture corpus, with fz-kdt.104(s) EXACT landed rule (indistinguishable AND strictly covered), instrumented at dispatch_from_callable_flow_edges: 12 distinct flow-plan shapes across 9 fixtures carry droppable edges, 18 edges by count. Worst: 00277_enum_tier0_fixture arms=11 drop=3 and arms=4 drop=2; behavior/enum_hof_three_distinct_closures arms=3 drop=2; behavior/enum_take_drop_split arms=3 drop=2. The rest are arms=2 drop=1 (00183, 00230, 00418, 00419, 00420, behavior/enum_take_drop_split, behavior/unused_range_binding).
Residual after such a drop: 12 shapes across 8 fixtures keep EQUAL-denotation twins (nocover=0 everywhere -- the fz-kdt.107 no-cover class does NOT appear on this path), e.g. 00277 arms=9 equal=3, behavior/enum_map_family arms=9 equal=3, behavior/fz_f98_range_map_converges arms=6 equal=2. Equal-denotation twins are a separate question (same denotation, different edge identity) and are NOT what this ticket is about.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN fz-kdt.104 (deliberate, recorded): dispatch_from_callable_flow_edges returns only the plan, and its body_ids index CallableConstructionFact members, built in parallel from the same flow.first_class_edges (jobs/transport.rs, the members field beside the selection field). Dropping an edge from the plan alone leaves the member -- and therefore its boundary and its executable demand -- standing, so the fix is not the same one-line filter: either the surviving rows keep their ORIGINAL body_id while dropped rows are omitted (plan-only shrink, member kept, resolution still demanded), or members and selection shrink together and every consumer of CallableConstructionMember has to agree. Neither was in scope for a P1 miscompile fix and neither is measured.

FIRST STEP: establish whether this is live. fz-kdt.104(s) LIFO recipe (Agenda::pop -> pop_back, agenda.rs) plus the 9 fixtures above; 00183 is already correct under LIFO after fz-kdt.104, so the callsite half was the whole P1 miscompile on that fixture. Find a fixture where the FLOW plan order alone changes behavior, or prove none exists and re-price this as artifact hygiene.

comments.text: RIDER (fz-kdt.106 landed, a010532e8, 2026-09-01): 106 changes this ticket's input -- re-measure the callable-flow edge population (was 18 edges) on the post-106 base before scoping; dominance absorption alters which correlated rows exist at the callable-flow surfaces.

COLD-REVIEW FINDINGS FOLDED (fz-kdt.107 review, 2026-09-01 at
788c0c21f):

(1) THIS TICKET OWNS enum_map_family's FIFO/LIFO canon gap -- the last
big schedule-visible surface post-kdt.106. 570 of its ~1,504 diff lines
sit under `selection` (this constructor's plan), and the movement is
whole-family BLOCKS across DIFFERENT question classes (FIFO's a0..a2
rows appear at LIFO's a3..a5) -- cross-class EDGE ORDER, not
within-class arm order. A within-class canonicalization is a measured
no-op on it (option C changed its canon by 0 lines).

(2) DIRECT CANONICALIZATION OF THE PLAN IS IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION
(verified by panic): pattern_dispatch_from_source requires monotonically
increasing body_id (SourcePattern(NonMonotonicBodyId)), and body_id
simultaneously indexes the parallel CallableConstructionFact.members
list -- row order and body numbering are welded. The sound fix is a
canonical order on flow.first_class_edges UPSTREAM
(jobs/runtime_demand.rs:~1155), BEFORE both members and selection are
derived, so there is one ordering authority and everything downstream
inherits it.

(3) The drop half of this ticket (18 droppable edges) inherits
fz-kdt.118's soundness question (observable-surface containment across
fun_top-erased closure positions) -- sequence after 118's verdict.

title: Callable-flow selection plans carry the same arm-order-is-semantics trap fz-kdt.104 fixed for callsites
